name: HTML
tagline: The standard markup language for structuring web content.
timeTravelLog: Discovered in 1991 at CERN by Tim Berners-Lee. It was designed to share linked documents across the world.
overview: HTML is the standard markup language for creating web pages. It defines the structure of a web page using elements and tags, serving as the skeleton upon which CSS styles and JavaScript logic are applied.

syllabus.title: Module 3: Links & Navigation
syllabus.desc: Create hyperlinks between pages and external sites.
syllabus.content: The <a> (anchor) tag creates hyperlinks. The href attribute defines the destination — a full URL, a relative page path, or a section ID on the current page using a # hash. Using target="_blank" opens the link in a new tab.
syllabus.codeExample: MDN Web Docs ↗ About Go to Services Section
syllabus.interactiveTip: Always add rel="noopener noreferrer" when using target="_blank" to prevent security vulnerabilities from malicious third-party pages!

syllabus.title: Module 4: Containers (Divs vs Spans)
syllabus.desc: Group page elements using block and inline structural wrappers.
syllabus.content: Use <div> — a block-level box that occupies the full row width — and <span> — an inline tag for highlighting small runs of text without disrupting flow. Both are neutral containers styled entirely by CSS.

syllabus.title: Module 5: Semantic HTML (Header, Footer, Main, Section, Article)
syllabus.desc: Writing meaningful HTML that communicates structure to both humans and machines.
syllabus.content: Semantic elements carry meaning beyond visual layout. <header> marks site navigation, <main> wraps the core content, <section> groups related topics, <article> represents standalone content, and <footer> holds supporting information. These improve SEO and screen-reader accessibility.

syllabus.interactiveTip: Semantic HTML improves search engine ranking by giving crawlers exact context about your page structure. Always prefer semantic elements over generic divs!

syllabus.title: Module 6: Forms & Inputs (Forms, Inputs, Labels, Buttons)
syllabus.desc: Capture user input through accessible form controls.
syllabus.content: HTML forms (<form>) collect user data and send it via HTTP. Inside forms, <input> elements capture text, numbers, checkboxes, radios, and passwords. <label> tags improve accessibility by linking visible text to input controls. <button> submits or triggers form actions.
syllabus.codeExample:
<form action="/send" method="POST">
  <label for="user-name">Name:</label>
  <input type="text" id="user-name" name="name" placeholder="Enter name...">
  
  <label for="role">Role:</label>
  <select id="role" name="role">
    <option value="designer">DESIGNER</option>
    <option value="developer">DEVELOPER</option>
  </select>
  
  <button type="submit">SUBMIT</button>
</form>
syllabus.interactiveTip: Always pair <label> elements with <input> using matching 'for' and 'id' attributes. This allows clicking the label to focus the input field!

syllabus.title: Module 7: Metadata & SEO (Head Tags, Favicons & SEO)
syllabus.desc: Configure head tags for browsers and search engines.
syllabus.content: The <head> element contains the page's metadata. It includes <title> (the browser tab text), <meta> tags for descriptions, keywords and viewport, <link> tags for stylesheets and favicons, and structured data scripts. These signals directly influence how your page appears in search results.
syllabus.codeExample:
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Dashboard | Your Name</title>
  <meta name="description" content="A clear, accessible project dashboard.">
  <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/css/style.css">
</head>
syllabus.interactiveTip: The meta viewport tag is critical for mobile responsiveness! Without it, mobile browsers render your page at desktop width and scale it down, making text tiny.

quiz.question: What does HTML stand for?
quiz.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language — the standard language used to structure and define the content of web pages.

quiz.question: Which HTML tag is used to create a hyperlink?
quiz.explanation: The <a> (anchor) tag creates hyperlinks. Its 'href' attribute specifies the destination URL or page path.

quiz.question: Which semantic element represents the primary content area of a page?
quiz.explanation: <main> is the semantic element that wraps the dominant, unique content of the page — there should only be one per document.

quest.title: Project: Build a Dashboard Page
quest.challenge: Build a complete page structure with semantic tags, a form, an image, and proper meta information in the head.
instructions: 1. Add a <header> with an <h1> title for your website.
2. Add a <main> section containing an <article> with a project description.
3. Add an tag showing a sample image from any public URL.
4. Create a <form> with a text input for a user name and a submit button.
5. Wrap everything properly and verify your semantic structure.
